q: What is the earliest age at which you can get a Missouri instruction permit?
exp: Missouri's Graduated Driver License program starts with the instruction permit at age 15.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, GDL Step One, p. 15

q: How many questions are on the Missouri Class F written test?
exp: The Class F written test has 25 multiple choice questions taken from the Driver Guide.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), p. 2 and Ch. 2, Written Test, p. 18; MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: How many written test questions must you answer correctly to pass in Missouri?
exp: You need 20 of 25 correct, which is 80 percent, so you can miss no more than 5.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), p. 2; MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: On the Missouri road sign test, what must you do to pass?
b: Correctly identify at least 3 of 6 signs
c: Correctly identify at least 4 of 6 signs
d: Correctly identify at least 8 of 10 signs
exp: The sign recognition test shows six signs, and you pass by identifying at least four.
src: 12 CSR 10-24.452 (sign recognition test)

q: Maya is 15 and has her instruction permit. Who may sit beside her while she drives?
c: A licensed 22-year-old friend with no written permission from her parents
d: Any licensed adult riding in the back seat
exp: Under 16, the front seat companion must be a parent, stepparent, grandparent, legal guardian, qualified driving instructor, or a licensed person at least 25 with three years of driving and the parent's written permission.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Permit Notes, p. 15

q: You are 16 and hold a Missouri instruction permit. Who may supervise your driving?
a: A licensed driver at least 21 years old in the front seat
b: A licensed driver at least 18 years old in the front seat
c: A licensed driver at least 25 years old in any seat
d: Only a parent or legal guardian
exp: From age 16, any licensed driver at least 21 may ride in the front seat with a permit holder.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Permit Notes, p. 15

q: How much driving instruction must you complete before getting a Missouri intermediate license?
a: 40 hours, including at least 5 at night
b: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night
d: 40 hours, including at least 10 at night
exp: The 40 required hours must include at least ten hours of nighttime driving.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, To Graduate to an Intermediate License, p. 16

q: How long must you hold a Missouri instruction permit before you can get an intermediate license?
exp: The permit must be held at least six months (182 days), starting the day after it is issued.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, p. 16

q: During the first six months on a Missouri intermediate license, how many passengers under 19 who are not immediate family may ride with you?
exp: For the first six months, the limit is one passenger under 19 who is not a member of your immediate family.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: Between which hours may a Missouri intermediate license holder not drive alone, unless an exception applies?
exp: Intermediate drivers may not drive alone from 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. except for a school activity, job or emergency, or with a licensed driver 21 or older.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: After six months on a Missouri intermediate license, how many passengers under 19 who are not immediate family may you carry?
exp: After the first six months, the limit rises to three passengers under 19 who are not immediate family.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: An intermediate license holder needs to drive home from a late shift at work at 1:30 a.m. with no one else in the car. Is this allowed?
a: No, never between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m.
b: Only with a signed note from a parent
c: Yes, driving to or from a job is an exception
exp: Driving to and from a school activity, a job or an emergency is an exception to the 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. limit.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: Which passenger lets an intermediate driver drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. for any reason?
d: A brother or sister of any age
exp: The late night limit does not apply when a licensed driver 21 or older rides along.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: For the intermediate license passenger limit, which passenger does NOT count toward the limit?
a: Your 17-year-old sister who lives with you
exp: Immediate family, such as brothers and sisters living in your household, does not count toward the passenger limit.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Driving Restrictions, p. 16

q: To trade an intermediate license for a full license at 18, which record do you need?
a: No traffic conviction in the last 6 months only
b: No crash of any kind since getting the permit
c: No more than 4 points on your record
d: No alcohol-related offense or traffic conviction in the last 12 months
exp: A full under-21 license requires no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last 12 months.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Step Three, p. 17

q: Which tests do you take when moving from an intermediate license to a full Missouri license?
b: All four parts of the exam
c: The vision and road sign tests
exp: You pass the vision and road sign recognition tests; the written and driving tests are not repeated.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Step Three, p. 17

q: What is the minimum vision sharpness standard for a Missouri license?
exp: The standard minimum acuity is at least 20/40 with either or both eyes, with lenses if you need them.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Vision Test, pp. 18 to 19

q: What side (peripheral) vision does Missouri require?
a: At least 55 degrees in each eye or 85 degrees in one eye
b: At least 45 degrees in each eye
c: At least 70 degrees in each eye
d: At least 140 degrees in one eye
exp: The standard peripheral reading is at least 55 degrees in each eye or 85 degrees in one eye.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Vision Test, p. 19

q: You fail the Missouri written test in the morning. When may you try again?
a: Not until the next business day
d: The same day; you may take it up to two times a day
exp: The Highway Patrol lets you take the written test up to two times per day until you pass.
src: MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: How many Missouri driving tests may you take in one day?
exp: Only one driving test is allowed per day.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Failing the Driving Test, p. 21; MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: What happens after you fail the Missouri driving test three times?
a: You must wait one year and restart with a new permit
b: You need more behind the wheel training and DOR approval before testing again
c: You must retake only the written test
d: Nothing changes; you may keep testing once a day
exp: After three failures, the DOR requires proof of additional training and gives approval before another test.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Failing the Driving Test, p. 21

q: How much does the Highway Patrol charge for the non-commercial written and driving tests?
exp: Non-CDL written and skills tests are free; you pay when you buy the permit or license at a license office.
src: MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: What is the DOR fee for a Missouri instruction permit?
exp: The Class F instruction permit costs $10, plus the license office processing fee.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Permit Fees, p. 8; DOR, The Missouri Driver License (dor.mo.gov/driver-license/resources/license.html)

q: What is the DOR fee for a Missouri intermediate license?
exp: The intermediate license costs $14 and is valid up to two years.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, License Fees, p. 8; DOR, The Missouri Driver License (dor.mo.gov/driver-license/resources/license.html)

q: In Missouri, who gives the written, vision, road sign and driving tests?
exp: The Highway Patrol administers the driver examination; the Department of Revenue issues the permit or license.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Where to Take the Exam, p. 18

q: You just passed the written, vision and road sign tests. May you drive with your test result form?
a: No, you must first get the permit at a license office
c: Yes, if a parent rides with you
exp: The driver examination record is not valid as a permit or license. Take it to a license office to get the permit.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3

q: How long is a Missouri instruction permit valid?
a: 6 months, and it cannot be renewed
d: Up to 12 months, and you may renew it without retesting
exp: The permit is valid up to 12 months, and it can be renewed as often as needed without new written tests.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, pp. 8 and 15

q: How many proofs of Missouri residency do you need for a REAL ID-compliant license?
exp: A REAL ID-compliant document needs two residency documents; a non-REAL ID card needs one.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Missouri Residency, p. 7

q: A new Missouri resident has a valid license from another state. Which tests must the driver take?
b: The vision and road sign tests
c: All four parts of the exam
exp: Transferring a valid out-of-state license, or one expired no more than 184 days, requires only the vision and road sign tests.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, p. 6; Ch. 2, p. 18

q: A new resident's out-of-state license expired 200 days ago. What must the driver do in Missouri?
c: Take only the road sign test
d: Pay a late fee and transfer it
exp: An out-of-state license expired more than 184 days requires the written, vision, road sign and driving tests.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, p. 6

q: How large is the parallel parking space on the Missouri driving test?
exp: You park in a space 25 feet long and seven feet wide.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 20

q: On the Missouri driving test, how close to the curb must you park?
exp: Both the parallel park and the hill park are scored on stopping no more than 18 inches from the curb.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 20

q: How many points can you lose on the Missouri driving test before you fail?
exp: The examiner subtracts points for errors, and losing more than 30 points is a failed test.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Your Grade, p. 21

q: Who may ride in the car during your Missouri driving test?
d: The examiner and a driving instructor
exp: You drive with the examiner beside you, and no one else may ride along.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 19

q: Who must wear a seat belt when a Missouri instruction permit holder drives?
b: The driver and the front seat passenger
exp: Seat belts must be worn by the driver and all passengers when a permit holder drives.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Permit Notes, p. 15

q: To get an intermediate license, how long must you go without a traffic conviction?
exp: The intermediate license requires no traffic convictions in the last six months and no alcohol-related convictions in the last 12 months.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, Step Two, p. 16

q: In how many languages does the Highway Patrol offer the Class F written test?
b: 20, plus a sign language video version
exp: The Patrol offers the Class F written test in 20 languages, including a sign language video version.
src: MSHP, Modernized Testing System: DOR-FUSION (statepatrol.dps.mo.gov)

q: What can happen if you use a phone or recording device during a Missouri driver test?
a: It is fraud and can cost you your driving privilege for up to one year
b: You lose 5 points on the test
c: You must wait 7 days to retest
d: Nothing, if you only check the time
exp: Using a recording or two-way communicating device during testing is fraud, a class A misdemeanor that may cost you your privilege for up to a year.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Fraud, p. 21

q: Elena holds a driver license from Brazil and moves to Missouri. What should she expect?
a: To take only the vision test
b: To transfer the license with no tests
c: To take only the road sign test
d: To take the written, vision, road sign and driving tests
exp: The vision and road sign shortcut covers licenses from other states. A new Missouri license otherwise requires the four-part exam.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, pp. 5 to 6

q: How long do you have to finish parallel parking on the Missouri driving test?
exp: One scored item is the ability to park the vehicle within two minutes.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 20

q: What is the minimum extra fine for a first offense of speeding or passing in a Missouri work zone on a state road?
exp: A first offense brings a fine of at least $250 on top of any other fine; later offenses at least $300.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, p. 22 and Ch. 7, p. 51 (RSMo 304.582)

q: What is the most you can be fined for holding a phone while driving in a Missouri work zone or school zone?
exp: Under the hands-free law, a violation in a work zone or school zone can cost up to $500.
src: RSMo 304.822 (summary, combswaterkotte.com; news.mobar.org)

q: A school patrol member at a Missouri school crossing signals you to stop. What must you do?
b: Slow down and go if no children are in the street
c: Stop only if a police officer is present
exp: At a school crossing with a traffic patrol, you must stop and yield when a patrol member signals you.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 4, p. 30

q: Who sets the school zone speed limit you must obey in Missouri?
d: The limit posted on signs by the city or state
exp: Missouri has no single statewide school zone speed; obey the slower posted limit when lights flash or children are present.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 4, p. 30

q: What is the minimum work zone fine for a second or later offense of speeding or passing in a Missouri work zone?
exp: Second and later offenses bring a fine of at least $300 on top of other fines.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, p. 51 (RSMo 304.582)

q: In a Missouri mobile work zone, what tells you which lane to move into?
b: A flashing arrow panel on a work vehicle
c: A white diamond on the pavement
d: Flashing red lights on the shoulder
exp: In a mobile work zone, a protective vehicle with a flashing arrow panel shows the lane to merge into.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Mobile Work Zone, p. 53

q: On the Missouri road sign test, what does an eight-sided sign always mean?
exp: The octagon is used only for the stop sign.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Sign Shapes, p. 45

q: A triangle pointing down, red and white, tells you to:
c: Watch for a lane that ends
d: Slow down and give the right of way to traffic you are entering or crossing
exp: The triangle is the yield sign: slow down and let traffic in the intersection or road you are entering go first.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Yield, p. 49

q: What does a five-sided sign shaped like a house warn you about?
c: A school zone or school crossing
exp: The pentagon shape marks school signs.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Sign Shapes, p. 45

q: A round yellow sign with a black X and two letters R tells you:
a: You are at the tracks now
exp: The round sign is the railroad advance warning sign, placed before the crossing.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Railroad Crossing, p. 50

q: The white X-shaped crossbuck at a railroad crossing has the same meaning as which sign?
exp: The crossbuck means you must yield to trains. A sign below it may show how many tracks there are.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, p. 51

q: What does a sideways yellow triangle, shaped like a pennant, on the left side of the road mark?
a: A sharp curve to the left
d: The start of a no passing zone
exp: The pennant shape is used only for the No Passing Zone sign.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Sign Shapes, p. 46

q: What color are construction and work zone signs?
c: Orange with black letters or symbols
exp: Work zone signs are fluorescent orange and warn of work on or beside the road.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Work Zone Signs, p. 51

q: A blue sign with white symbols points you to:
b: Motorist services such as rest areas, gas and hospitals
exp: Blue signs show motorist services.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Sign Colors and Service Signs, pp. 46 and 54

q: A brown sign with white letters guides you to:
exp: Brown signs point to public recreation and cultural interests, such as parks and museums.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Sign Colors, p. 46

q: What do green signs with white letters show?
exp: Green guide signs show direction and distance to cities, airports and state lines.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Guide Signs, p. 54

q: A yellow diamond sign with a traffic light symbol means:
a: The traffic signal ahead is broken
c: A traffic signal is ahead, so be ready to stop
exp: The Signal Ahead sign warns of a traffic light on the road you are on.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Warning Signs, p. 46

q: A yellow diamond with a car and wavy skid marks behind it warns that:
a: The road ahead winds back and forth
b: The road ahead is slippery when wet
c: Loose gravel is on the shoulder
exp: The Slippery When Wet sign warns that the road becomes unusually slick in wet weather.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Special Road and Traffic Conditions, p. 47

q: A yellow diamond shows two lanes joining, with a broken line ending on the right. What should a driver in the right lane do?
a: Merge left, yielding to traffic in the left lane
b: Speed up to stay ahead of the left lane
c: Stop and wait for a gap
d: Expect traffic from the left to merge right
exp: The Lane Ends sign means two lanes become one; drivers in the ending lane merge and yield.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Lane Ends/Merge Left, p. 47

q: What is the difference between a Turn sign and a Curve sign?
a: A Curve sign marks the sharper bend
b: A Turn sign is used only on interstates
d: A Turn sign marks a sharper, slower bend
exp: A turn sign warns of a sharp bend where the safe speed is lower; a curve sign marks a gentler bend.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Turns and Curves, p. 47

q: A yellow diamond shows an arrow bending sharply right, then sharply left. What does it warn of?
a: A road that splits in two
c: Two sharp turns in opposite directions
exp: The Reverse Turn sign warns of two turns in opposite directions; the second may be sharper than the first.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Reverse Turn, p. 47

q: A yellow sign with one large black arrow on the outside of a bend tells you to:
b: Slow down for a sharp change of direction
d: Turn only in the arrow's direction at the next street
exp: The Large Arrow sign stands on the outside of a turn and warns of a sharp change of direction.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Large Arrow, p. 47

q: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a farm vehicle means it:
exp: The slow moving vehicle emblem marks vehicles going less than 25 mph.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Slow Moving Vehicle, p. 48

q: A yellow diamond shows a T shape. What is ahead?
a: A crossroad where traffic crosses your path
b: A side road joins from one side
d: The road you are on ends; you must turn right or left
exp: The T Intersection sign means the road does not continue, so you must turn right or left.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Road Intersections, p. 48

q: A sign shows a red circle with a slash over a U-shaped arrow. What does it mean?
exp: A red circle with a slash means the action shown is not allowed.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 48

q: You see a red and white sign reading WRONG WAY. What should you do?
a: Keep going to the next exit
b: Pull off the road, turn around and go back as soon as it is safe
c: Stop in your lane and wait for help
d: Back up slowly to the last intersection
exp: Wrong Way means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic. Get off the road, turn around and go back.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Wrong Way, p. 49

q: A sign reads SPEED LIMIT 70 above MINIMUM 40 on an interstate. In normal conditions, which speed breaks the law?
exp: Interstates have a minimum speed. Under normal conditions you may not drive slower than 40 mph.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Speed Limit, p. 50

q: On an interstate route sign, what does an odd number such as I-35 usually tell you?
a: The route runs east and west
b: The route loops around a city
c: The route is a toll road
d: The route runs north and south
exp: North-south routes have odd numbers; east-west routes have even numbers.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Route Signs, p. 54

q: What does a three-digit interstate number starting with an even digit, such as I-270, usually mean?
b: A route running north and south
exp: Loops around cities have three-digit numbers that begin with an even digit; spurs into a city begin with an odd digit.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Route Signs, p. 54

q: How often are emergency reference markers placed along Missouri interstates?
exp: Reference markers stand every 0.2 mile, so a marker is always in sight to tell responders where you are.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Emergency Reference Markers, p. 54

q: A yellow diamond reads SOFT SHOULDER. What should you do?
a: Stay on the pavement, because the shoulder is soft
b: Use the shoulder to pass slow traffic
c: Pull onto the shoulder to let others pass
d: Expect a lane to be added
exp: The shoulder ahead is soft; do not drive off the pavement.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Soft Shoulder, p. 48

q: A yellow diamond shows a small arrow joining a larger line from the side, with no lane ending. What should you expect?
a: Your lane ends and you must merge
c: A one lane bridge is ahead
d: Vehicles from another road may move into your lane
exp: The Merge sign warns that traffic from another road will enter; be ready for vehicles moving into your lane.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Merge, p. 47

q: What does a yellow diamond reading ADDED LANE tell you?
c: Entering traffic gets its own new lane, so no merging is needed
d: The right lane is for passing
exp: An added lane lets traffic from another road enter without merging.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Added Lane, p. 47

q: A red circle with a white bar across it and the words DO NOT ENTER stands at a road opening. What does it mean?
a: The road is closed to trucks only
b: You may not drive into that road from where you are
c: Enter only after a full stop
exp: Do Not Enter marks roads and ramps you may not drive into from your direction.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Do Not Enter, p. 49

q: An orange diamond reads ROAD WORK AHEAD. What should you do?
a: Slow down and watch for workers, equipment and lane changes
b: Speed up to get through quickly
d: Use the shoulder to pass slower cars
exp: Orange work zone signs warn that work is being done on or beside the road ahead.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Work Zone Signs, p. 51

q: A yellow diamond shows two arrows, one pointing up and one pointing down. What does it warn?
d: Two-way traffic ahead, with oncoming cars in the next lane
exp: The Two Way Traffic sign warns that you are leaving a one way or divided road and will meet oncoming traffic.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, End Divided Roadway, p. 47; MUTCD 11th ed. W6-3

q: A yellow diamond shows a person holding a flag or paddle. What is ahead?
c: A flagger who may tell you to stop or go slowly
exp: Flaggers control traffic in work zones; follow their instructions.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Flagging Operation, p. 53

q: In Missouri, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
a: Only when a green arrow is also lit
b: Without stopping, if no one is coming
c: Never; Missouri bans right turns on red
d: After a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and traffic, unless a sign forbids it
exp: After a complete stop, you may turn right on red if the way is clear, unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Traffic Signals, p. 44; RSMo 304.281

q: You are on a one-way street at a red light, and the cross street is also one-way to the left. May you turn left on red in Missouri?
b: Yes, without stopping if the way is clear
c: No, Missouri law allows only a right turn on red
d: Yes, but only between midnight and 5 a.m.
exp: Missouri's signal law permits only a right turn on a steady red; it has no left on red rule.

q: You face a steady red arrow in Missouri. When may you turn?
a: After a complete stop, if the way is clear
b: Only after the signal shows a green arrow or a flashing yellow arrow
c: Right away, if no pedestrians are present
exp: At a steady red arrow, stop and wait for a green light or a flashing yellow arrow.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Left Turn Signals, p. 44

q: A Missouri intersection has a NO TURN ON RED sign. What must you do at a red light?
a: Wait for the signal to turn green before turning right
b: Turn right after a full stop if clear
c: Turn right only if no cars are coming
d: Turn right only from the center lane
exp: A posted No Right Turn on Red sign cancels the right turn on red.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Traffic Signals, p. 44

q: Under Missouri's Move Over law, what must you do when passing a stopped tow truck with flashing amber lights on a four-lane highway?
a: Move to a lane not next to it if safe, or slow down
b: Nothing, because the law covers only police cars
c: Stop behind it until it leaves
exp: The law covers stopped vehicles with red, red and blue, amber, or amber and white lights. Change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow down.
src: MoDOT, Missouri's Move Over Law; RSMo 304.022

q: A Missouri school bus stops with red lights flashing on a two-lane road. Where must you stop?
b: Only if you are behind the bus
c: Beside the bus, so children can see you
exp: Oncoming and following traffic must stop before reaching the bus; Missouri sets no exact distance.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, School Buses, p. 23

q: How many points does a Missouri driver get for illegally passing a stopped school bus?
exp: Failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students adds five points.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, p. 24 and Ch. 11, p. 74

q: On a Missouri four-lane highway, a school bus stops with red lights flashing on the other side. Must you stop?
a: Yes, all traffic must always stop
b: No, traffic going the opposite way on four or more lanes need not stop
c: Yes, unless a police officer waves you on
exp: Traffic traveling the opposite direction need not stop on a divided highway or a road of four or more lanes.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, School Buses, p. 24

q: When do the amber warning lights on a Missouri school bus begin flashing?
a: About 500 feet before the bus stops
b: About 100 feet before the bus stops
c: Only after the bus has stopped
d: When the stop arm folds in
exp: Amber lights flash 500 feet before the bus comes to a designated stop.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, School Buses, p. 23

q: What is the first offense penalty for illegally passing a stopped school bus in Missouri?
d: 5 points, a fine up to $1,000 and a 90-day suspension
exp: A first offense brings five points and a court-ordered 90-day suspension; fines can reach $1,000.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, p. 24; Missourinet, Aug. 24, 2026

q: An ambulance with a siren approaches while you are in the middle of a Missouri intersection. What should you do?
a: Stop at once in the intersection
b: Back up out of the intersection
c: Drive through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop
exp: If you are in an intersection, drive through it before you pull over to the right.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, Emergency Vehicles, p. 23

q: On a Missouri one-way street, a fire truck with a siren comes up behind you. Which way do you pull over?
a: To the nearest edge, left or right
b: As far to the right as possible
c: To the left, away from the curb
d: Stay in your lane and speed up
exp: Missouri law tells drivers to pull as far to the right as possible and stop; it gives no left side option.
src: RSMo 304.022.1; MO Driver Guide, Ch. 3, p. 23

q: An emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside a roundabout. What should you do?
a: Leave at your exit, then pull to the right
exp: Never stop in a roundabout. Exit, then pull over to the right.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, Roundabouts, Emergency Vehicles, p. 27

q: What kind of offense is breaking Missouri's Move Over or emergency vehicle law?
c: A felony on the first offense
exp: Violation of section 304.022 is a class A misdemeanor.
src: RSMo 304.022 (Justia, 2025)

q: How far ahead should you signal before turning in Missouri?
exp: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, p. 24 and Ch. 8, p. 58

q: In Missouri, where is a U-turn illegal?
a: At an intersection controlled by a traffic signal
c: On a residential street with no sign
d: At an intersection with no signal or officer
exp: Never make a U-turn where a No U-Turn sign is posted or at an intersection controlled by a signal or police officer.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 25

q: A side driveway lies between you and the street where you plan to turn right. When should you signal?
b: Only once you are in the turn
c: You do not need to signal
exp: If there are other streets or driveways before your turn, wait until you have passed them to signal.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, Signal When You Change Direction, p. 58

q: Why does Missouri forbid U-turns on curves and near the top of a hill?
b: Those spots are reserved for passing
c: Other drivers may not see your vehicle in time
exp: U-turns should not be made on a curve or near a hill crest where other drivers may not see you.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 25

q: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection. May you make a U-turn there in Missouri?
a: Yes, if the officer is not looking
c: Yes, if no sign forbids it
exp: U-turns are not allowed at intersections controlled by a traffic signal or a police officer.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 25

q: How far may you travel in a Missouri two-way left-turn lane?
exp: A two-way left-turn lane is not a travel lane; a vehicle may not travel in it for more than 500 feet.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 3, Two-Way Left-Turn Lanes, p. 26

q: What following distance does the Missouri Driver Guide teach in normal conditions?
exp: Use the three second rule: count three seconds after the car ahead passes a fixed point.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, Three Second Rule, p. 57

q: Unless signs say otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Missouri city, town or village?
exp: The speed limit in any city, town or village is 25 mph unless another limit is posted.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Speed Limit, p. 50

q: What is the slowest speed allowed on a Missouri interstate in normal conditions?
exp: You may not drive slower than 40 mph on interstate highways under normal conditions.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Speed Limit, p. 50

q: How much following distance does the Missouri Driver Guide advise on snow or ice?
exp: On snow or ice, leave about eight to ten seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 9, Winter Driving, p. 63

q: What is the maximum speed on Missouri lettered roads, such as Route K, unless posted otherwise?
exp: Lettered roads have a maximum of 55 mph.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Roadway Maximum Speed table, p. 50

q: What is the maximum speed on Missouri rural expressways unless posted otherwise?
exp: Rural expressways have a maximum of 65 mph.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Roadway Maximum Speed table, p. 50

q: How many points does a speeding conviction under Missouri state law add to your record?
exp: Speeding under state law adds 3 points; under a city or county ordinance it adds 2.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, p. 73; RSMo 302.302

q: What is the maximum speed on interstates inside Missouri's urbanized areas unless posted otherwise?
exp: Interstates, freeways and expressways within urbanized areas have a 60 mph maximum.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 7, Roadway Maximum Speed table, p. 50

q: On a Missouri two-way street, which side may you park on?
a: Only the right side, facing the way traffic moves
exp: Do not park on the left side of a two-way street or with your vehicle facing against traffic.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 5, No-Parking Zones, p. 35

q: What is the fine range for parking illegally in a Missouri disability space?
exp: Violators are fined no less than $50 and no more than $300.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 5, International Symbol of Access, p. 36

q: In Missouri, may you park beside a curb painted yellow?
d: Yes, if you stay in the car
exp: The Driver Guide lists a curb painted yellow as a no-parking zone.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 5, No-Parking Zones, p. 35

q: You have a disability placard, but the disabled person is not with you. May you park in a disability space in Missouri?
a: Yes, if the placard is displayed
d: Yes, if no other spaces are open
exp: The space may be used only when the disabled person is riding, or being dropped off or picked up.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 35 to 36

q: What does Missouri law require when you pass a bicycle going your way?
a: Pass within 1 foot to save time
b: Leave a safe distance and stay clear until you are well past it
exp: Drivers must leave a safe distance when passing a bicycle and stay clear until safely past it.
src: RSMo 304.678 (Justia, 2025)

q: How much room does the Missouri Driver Guide tell you to give a bicycle or moped when passing?
exp: Give bicycles and mopeds a full lane width; if the lane is too narrow to share, wait for a clear stretch.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 4, Mopeds and Bicycles, p. 31

q: In Missouri, passing a bicycle too closely is what kind of offense if no crash occurs?
exp: Breaking the bicycle passing rule is an infraction, or a class C misdemeanor if a crash results.
src: RSMo 304.678 (Justia, 2025)

q: In Missouri, when must your headlights be on?
b: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
c: From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise
exp: Lamps must be lit from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and in poor visibility or bad weather.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 9, Night Driving, p. 62; RSMo 307.020

q: In Missouri, you must switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
exp: Use low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and within 300 feet when following.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 9, Night Driving, p. 62

q: Within how many days must a Missouri crash involving an uninsured driver, with an injury, be reported in writing to the Department of Revenue?
exp: The report is due within 30 days after the crash.
src: RSMo 303.040 (Justia, 2025)

q: In Missouri, how far ahead must you be able to see people and vehicles clearly before daytime headlights are required?
exp: Headlights are required whenever there is not enough light to see persons and vehicles clearly 500 feet ahead.

q: You turn on your windshield wipers because of rain in Missouri. What else must you do?
exp: You must use your headlights any time the weather requires your wipers.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 9, Headlight Use, p. 62

q: When following another vehicle at night in Missouri, within what distance must you use low beams?
exp: Use low beams when following another vehicle within 300 feet.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 9, Night Driving, p. 62

q: How many points are added for leaving the scene of a crash under Missouri state law?
exp: Leaving the scene of an accident under state law adds 12 points and can lead to revocation.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, p. 73; RSMo 302.302

q: In Missouri, which crashes must be reported in writing to the Department of Revenue?
d: Ones with an uninsured driver where someone is hurt or killed, or damage is over $500
exp: A written report is due within 30 days for crashes with an uninsured motorist that injure or kill someone or cause over $500 damage.
src: RSMo 303.040 (Justia, 2025)

q: During a traffic stop in Missouri, you have a firearm in the car. When should you tell the officer?
exp: If you have a weapon in the vehicle, inform the officer upon first contact.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, When Stopped by Law Enforcement, p. 60

q: What does signing a Missouri traffic ticket mean?
b: It is not an admission of guilt
c: You give up your right to court
d: You agree to pay at once
exp: Signing a ticket is not an admission of guilt, but refusing to sign may lead to arrest.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, p. 61

q: What does the Missouri Driver Guide say your passengers should do during a traffic stop?
a: Stay calm, stay in the car and keep their hands in view
b: Get out and stand by the road
d: Record the officer on their phones
exp: Passengers should remain calm, stay in the vehicle and keep their hands in plain view; no one should use a phone.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, p. 60

q: At what BAC is a Missouri driver under 21 subject to losing the license?
exp: For minors, a BAC of .02 percent or more brings the same administrative action as .08 for adults.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Administrative Actions, p. 67; DOR Administrative Alcohol FAQs

q: What happens if you refuse a chemical test when a Missouri officer suspects DWI?
b: Your license is suspended for 30 days
c: Your license is revoked for one year
d: You must retake the written test only
exp: Refusing a chemical test results in a one-year revocation.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Refusal, p. 70; DOR DWI page

q: Under Missouri's hands-free law, which is allowed while driving?
a: Holding the phone to read a text
b: A hands-free call using a single touch to answer
c: Typing a message at a red light while moving slowly
d: Watching a video while driving on the interstate
exp: Hands-free use, including a single tap or swipe, is allowed; holding or supporting the phone is not.
src: RSMo 304.822 (summary, combswaterkotte.com; news.mobar.org)

q: What is the illegal BAC for a Missouri driver 21 or older?
exp: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or more; 0.04 for commercial drivers and 0.02 if under 21.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Alcohol, p. 71

q: What is the illegal BAC for a commercial vehicle driver in Missouri?
exp: Commercial vehicle drivers are limited to 0.04 percent.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Alcohol, p. 71

q: To get a Missouri license back after a chemical test refusal, which is required?
c: A $45 fee, a SATOP program and two years of SR-22 insurance proof
exp: Reinstatement requires a $45 fee, a Substance Awareness Traffic Offender Program and proof of insurance (SR-22) for two years.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Reinstatement Requirements, p. 70

q: What is the most jail time for a first DWI conviction in Missouri?
exp: A first offense brings up to six months in jail and up to a $500 fine.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Court-Convicted Actions, p. 68

q: What license action follows a first DWI or BAC conviction in Missouri?
exp: A first DWI or BAC conviction brings a 90-day suspension; a restricted privilege may be available.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, p. 68; DOR DWI page

q: How many points does a first DWI conviction add in Missouri?
exp: A first DWI or BAC conviction adds 8 points; a second adds 12.
src: RSMo 302.302 (Justia, 2025)

q: Under Missouri's Abuse and Lose law, how long can a driver under 21 lose the license for using alcohol while driving?
exp: Abuse and Lose allows a 90-day loss of license for under-21 alcohol or drug offenses tied to driving or altering a license.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, Abuse and Lose, p. 69

q: What is the license penalty for a first Minor in Possession offense in Missouri?
exp: MIP brings a 30-day suspension the first time, 90 days the second and a one-year revocation the third.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, MIP, p. 69

q: What is the license penalty for a third Minor in Possession offense in Missouri?
exp: A third MIP offense brings a one-year revocation.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, MIP, p. 69

q: A 19-year-old changes the birth date on a license to buy alcohol in Missouri. What can happen?
a: Only a small fine; the license is safe
b: Nothing, if no alcohol is bought
c: A warning letter to the parents only
d: The license can be taken away
exp: Altering or misusing a license to buy alcohol is a reason for losing your license, and it falls under Abuse and Lose.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 1, p. 14 and Ch. 10, p. 69

q: What is the fine for a first violation of Missouri's hands-free law?
exp: A first offense costs up to $150, a second up to $250 and a third or later up to $500 within 24 months.
src: RSMo 304.822 (news.mobar.org; KBIA, Jan. 2, 2025)

q: May a Missouri officer pull you over only for holding your phone while driving?
a: Yes, it is a primary offense
b: No, the officer needs another reason to stop you
exp: Drivers cannot be stopped solely for a violation of the hands-free law.
src: RSMo 304.822 (news.mobar.org)

q: Does Missouri have a statewide law banning open containers of alcohol in passenger cars?
a: No, but many cities, such as St. Louis, ban them
b: Yes, for drivers and passengers everywhere
exp: Missouri has no uniform statewide open container law for passenger cars; local ordinances apply.
src: mccreadylaw.com, What Is Missouri's Open Container Law

q: Which drugs can lead to a DWI charge in Missouri if they impair your driving?
c: Only drugs taken without a prescription
exp: Missouri law does not distinguish between prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs when they impair driving.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 10, p. 71

q: Under Missouri law, who must wear a seat belt in every car?
a: The driver and front seat passengers
exp: Missouri requires the driver and front seat occupants to wear seat belts; children and passengers of intermediate drivers have extra rules.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, p. 55; RSMo 307.178

q: A 3-year-old who weighs 35 pounds rides in your car in Missouri. What is required?
exp: Children under 4, or under 40 pounds, must ride in a child passenger restraint system.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, Child Passenger Restraint Law, p. 55

q: How many points in 18 months lead to a Missouri license suspension?
exp: Eight or more points in 18 months brings a suspension: 30 days the first time, 60 the second and 90 after that.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, Racking Up Points, p. 73

q: When an intermediate license holder drives in Missouri, who must be belted?
exp: All passengers riding with an intermediate license holder must be properly restrained.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, p. 55

q: What is the most an adult can be fined for not wearing a seat belt in Missouri?
exp: The adult belt violation is an infraction with a fine of up to $10, no court costs and no points.

q: A 6-year-old weighs 50 pounds and is 4 feet tall. What must the child use in Missouri?
d: A child safety seat or booster seat
exp: Children 4 to 7 who weigh 40 to 79 pounds and are under 4 feet 9 inches need a child seat or booster seat.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 8, p. 56; RSMo 307.179

q: What is the fine for breaking Missouri's car seat or booster seat rule?
exp: The driver may be fined up to $50 plus court costs; the charge is dismissed if the driver shows a seat was obtained.
src: RSMo 307.179 (Justia, 2025)

q: What is Missouri's minimum liability insurance for injury to one person?
exp: Minimum limits are $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash for injuries and $25,000 for property damage.
src: RSMo 303.190 (Justia, 2025)

q: How many points does a conviction for driving without insurance add in Missouri?
exp: Failing to maintain financial responsibility adds 4 points.
src: RSMo 302.302 (Justia, 2025)

q: How many points in 12 months cause a one-year revocation in Missouri?
exp: Twelve or more points in 12 months, 18 in 24 months or 24 in 36 months bring a one-year revocation.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, p. 73

q: What does the Missouri DOR send when you reach 4 points in 12 months?
exp: Four points in 12 months brings an advisory letter, not a suspension.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, p. 73

q: After your Missouri license is reinstated following a point suspension, what happens to your point total?
exp: On reinstatement, the DOR reduces your total points to four; clean years reduce them further.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, How Points Come Off, p. 74

q: How many years without new points does it take for Missouri points to drop to zero?
exp: Points drop by one-third after one clean year, by half after two, and to zero after three.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 11, p. 74

q: Within how many days must a new Missouri resident register a vehicle?
exp: New residents must register their vehicles within 30 days of becoming Missouri residents.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 12, Registering Your Vehicle, p. 76

q: On the Missouri driving test, how many points must you lose to fail?
exp: Losing more than 30 points is a failed test.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Your Grade, p. 21

q: Which mistake fails the Missouri driving test at once?
d: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
exp: You fail immediately for a traffic violation, a crash that is your fault, hitting a pedestrian, dangerous driving or refusing to drive as asked.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Your Grade, p. 21

q: How many right and left turns are you asked to make on the Missouri driving test?
a: One right and one left turn
d: At least two right and two left turns
exp: The examiner asks for at least two right and two left turns.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 20

q: Does a poor parallel parking attempt alone fail the Missouri driving test?
b: Yes, if you take more than one try
c: No, it counts for only a few points
exp: Parallel parking counts for only a few points, and missing it does not automatically fail you.
src: MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: Which car may you use for the Missouri driving test?
a: Only a car registered in your own name
b: Any car that is properly registered and insured, even if it is not in your name
d: Only a car with an automatic transmission
exp: You provide the vehicle; it must be properly registered and insured but need not be in your name.
src: MSHP Driver Examination FAQs (apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov)

q: During the Missouri driving test hill park, what must you do?
a: Turn the wheels the correct way and set the parking brake
b: Leave the engine running in neutral
c: Park at least 3 feet from the curb
exp: The hill park is scored on wheel direction, gear, the parking brake and stopping no more than 18 inches from the curb.
src: MO Driver Guide (rev. Aug 2026), Ch. 2, Driving Test, p. 20
